project.name: DendrOSM
project.description: Quality assurance map of OSM trees.

tags.description: Trees shown on the map and checked.
Tree stumps shown on the map and checked.
Suggested by a QA check (and by "Fix with JOSM") in place of natural=tree for plants that are not trees, such as Agave americana.
Counted as a neighbour of a tree for the "Most isolated" record (distance from the nearest tree, wood or tree row).
Counted as a neighbour of a tree for the "Most isolated" record (distance from the nearest tree, wood or tree row).

Counted as a neighbour of a tree for the "Most isolated" record (distance from the nearest tree, wood or tree row). From zoom 16, a row with no natural=tree or natural=tree_stump among its nodes is filled with drawn trees (shape from leaf_type, colour from leaf_cycle, or both estimated from species/genus of the row).
Used for filtering, QA checks, the info panel and the Completeness tab (share of trees with species or genus). On natural=tree_row ways: estimate of leaf_type and leaf_cycle of the drawn trees.
Rendered with a white trunk (also with a variety, e.g. var. jacquemontii), on the map and in the trunk comparison drawing.
Rendered with an orange-red trunk, on the map and in the trunk comparison drawing.
Easter egg: rendered with a rainbow trunk, on the map and in the trunk comparison drawing.
Rendered with red fruits on the crown, in season (August–October in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with green fruits (walnuts) on the crown, in season (July–October in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with yellow fruits (lemons) on the crown, all year.
Rendered with orange fruits (bitter oranges) on the crown, in season (November–March in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with dark purple fruits (olives) on the crown, in season (October–December in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with orange-red fruits (persimmons) on the crown, in season (October–December in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with orange fruits on the crown, in season (November–April in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a rust-red crown in autumn (October–November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a crimson crown in autumn (October–November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a scarlet crown in autumn (October–November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a red crown in autumn (October–November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a golden yellow crown in autumn (November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a golden yellow crown in autumn (October–November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a russet crown in autumn (October–November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a russet crown in autumn (October–November in the northern hemisphere).
Rendered with a silver crown while in leaf (April–October in the northern hemisphere).

Rendered with a dull green crown with silvery spots, yellow with light spots in autumn, and with a light grey trunk (dark at the edges from 1.5 m of circumference), on the map and in the trunk comparison drawing, where the young trunk also has diamond-shaped lenticels.
Rendered with a blue-grey crown, all year.
Rendered with a silver-blue crown, all year.
Rendered with a silver-blue crown, all year.

Used for filtering, QA checks, the info panel and the Completeness tab (a tree with genus or species counts as having its taxon). On natural=tree_row ways: estimate of leaf_type and leaf_cycle of the drawn trees. A palm genus (Phoenix, Washingtonia, Trachycarpus…) or genus=Arecaceae makes the tree rendered as a palm. A common name of a genus (e.g. wierzba) is reported, and the 'Fix with JOSM' link writes the scientific name.

Shown in the info panel, with a hint that the tag does not say the rank; a QA check reports it when it points to another species or genus than species or genus; if the value is a species or a genus of the OSM wiki lists, the 'Fix with JOSM' link moves it to species or genus. Without genus and species, its first word is used as the genus to recognise palms, and leaf_type and leaf_cycle are estimated from it (as a genus if one word, otherwise as a species) for rendering.
Without species: a hint suggests species with the same Latin name, and the 'Fix with JOSM' link adds it.

Used for a QA check (taxon:xx without taxon); the same for the other languages. If the value is the name of a genus or of a species in the site's lists, or species is already present, genus:xx or species:xx is suggested and the 'Fix with JOSM' link moves it there.
Shown in the info panel (Variety). Suggested, with the 'Fix with JOSM' link, when species includes a variety (var. epithet) that is a taxon of variety rank on Wikidata.
Shown in the info panel (Cultivar). Suggested, with the 'Fix with JOSM' link, when species includes a cultivar (in quotation marks, or without after a species of the OSM wiki list).
Shown in the info panel (Variety) when taxon:variety is missing.
Shown in the info panel (Cultivar) when taxon:cultivar is missing.
Suggested by a QA check when wikipedia=* links the article of a genus.
Used for a hint (lowercase initial); the 'Fix with JOSM' link capitalises it.
Used for QA checks (also to find plants that are not trees, such as Q161115 Agave americana) and to show the common name in the info panel.
Used for hints: species:wikidata and species from the linked Wikidata item, when missing.

Used for a hint in the info panel (almost all values start with a capital letter). Without species: used for a QA check; if the value is the Italian name of a species in the site's list (e.g. Bagolaro), species is suggested and the 'Fix with JOSM' link adds it with the species tags; if it is the Italian name of a genus (e.g. Quercia), genus:it is suggested and the link moves it there.

Without species: used for a QA check; if the value is the English name of a genus in the OSM wiki list of genera or in the site's list (e.g. Poplar), genus:en is suggested. Suggested, and set by the 'Fix with JOSM' link, when species is the English name of a species in the site's list (species=American Chestnut -> species=Castanea dentata, species:en=American Chestnut).
Without species: used for a QA check; if the value is the French name of a genus in the OSM wiki list of genera, genus:fr is suggested.

Suggested instead of species:en when its value is the English name of a genus in the OSM wiki list of genera or in the site's list, and for the English name of a genus written in species (species=Birch -> genus=Betula, genus:en=Birch); set by the 'Fix with JOSM' link.

Without species: used for a QA check; if the value is the Japanese name of a genus in the site's list (e.g. ポプラ), genus:ja is suggested and the 'Fix with JOSM' link moves it there; if it is the Japanese standard name of a species (e.g. ケヤキ), species is suggested and the link adds it.
Suggested instead of species:ja when its value is the Japanese name of a genus in the site's list (e.g. ポプラ for Populus); set by the 'Fix with JOSM' link.
Suggested instead of species:fr when its value is the French name of a genus in the OSM wiki list of genera.

Without species: used for a QA check; if the value is the Polish name of a genus in the site's list, genus:pl is suggested and the 'Fix with JOSM' link moves it there; if it is the Polish name of a species (e.g. Dąb czerwony), species is suggested and the link adds it.

Suggested instead of species:pl when its value is the Polish name of a genus, and for the Polish name written in genus or species (genus=świerk -> genus=Picea, genus:pl=Świerk; species=Brzoza -> genus=Betula, genus:pl=Brzoza); set by the 'Fix with JOSM' link.
Suggested instead of species:it or taxon:it when its value is the Italian name of a genus (e.g. Pino); set by the 'Fix with JOSM' link.
Used for QA checks. Suggested instead of species:wikidata when that item has genus rank on Wikidata; set by the 'Fix with JOSM' link.

On natural=tree_row ways: shape of the drawn trees. Used to render the crown shape and the seasons (broadleaved deciduous trees take autumn colours; needleleaved deciduous ones are only drawn bare in winter), for QA checks and the Completeness tab (share of trees with the tag).
Rendered with a palm crown (lance-shaped fronds), without seasons. Reported by a QA check on trees that the OSM wiki lists give as broadleaved and that are neither palms nor palm-like plants.
The tree is rendered as a palm, even with leaf_type=broadleaved or needleleaved.
The tree is rendered as a palm, even with leaf_type=broadleaved or needleleaved.
The tree is rendered as a palm, even with leaf_type=broadleaved or needleleaved.
The tree is rendered as a palm, even with leaf_type=broadleaved or needleleaved.
The tree is rendered as a palm, even with leaf_type=broadleaved or needleleaved.

On natural=tree_row ways: colour and seasons of the drawn trees. Used to render the crown color and the seasons (deciduous trees take autumn colours in autumn and are drawn bare in winter, according to the viewer's date), for QA checks, the info panel and the Completeness tab (share of trees with the tag).
Used to render the trunk, for QA checks, a hint (MASAF minimum circumference, Italy), the Completeness and Record trees tabs.
Trunk diameter (millimetres without a unit): used like circumference when that is missing, and for QA checks (including the comparison with circumference).
Used for QA checks, to estimate the trunk size, in the Completeness tab (share of trees with the tag) and in the Record trees tab (tallest, most slender and stockiest tree).
Used to render the 2D crown, for QA checks, in the Completeness tab (share of trees with the tag) and in the Record trees tab (widest crown).
Used for QA checks.
Used to render the trees, for QA checks and for the world map of monumental trees.
Used to render the trees.
Used to estimate diameter_crown when missing.
Used to estimate diameter_crown when missing.
Used to estimate diameter_crown when missing.
Used to estimate diameter_crown when missing.
Used for QA checks (also: code not in the MASAF list, code of a single tree on several trees, code of a group on one tree only), hints and the info panel.
Used for QA checks, the info panel and a hint (criteria from the MASAF list when missing).

Homogeneous group of the MASAF list (e.g. type=site + natural=tree_group): the member natural=tree nodes are rendered as monumental trees, also on the world map of monumental trees, and their info panel shows the code with a link to the relation. The code also counts the MASAF tree as already on OSM.
On a relation with ref:masaf (homogeneous group): shown in the info panel of the member trees.
On a relation with ref:masaf (homogeneous group): shown in the info panel of the member trees.
Used for QA checks (also: tag outside Italy) and the info panel.
Tree of public interest in Portugal: used for QA checks and the info panel.
Protected tree in Luxembourg: used for QA checks and the info panel.
Shown in the info panel and used for QA checks (tag outside Portugal).
Natural monument in the Polish CRFOP register: used for QA checks and the info panel.
Natural monument in the Polish CRFOP register: used for QA checks and the info panel.
Memorial tree in the Czech ÚSOP register (DRUSOP database): used for QA checks (a monumental tree should have denotation=natural_monument; tag outside Czechia) and the info panel.
Tree in the Tree Register of Britain and Ireland: shown in the info panel, with a link to the tree's page on the register.
Treated as ref:TROBI: shown in the info panel, with a link to the tree's page on the register.
Champion tree: shown in the info panel with champion:territory, champion:category and champion:date.
Shown in the info panel for champion trees.
Shown in the info panel for champion trees.
Shown in the info panel for champion trees.

Counted in the Completeness tab for dioecious trees only (share of the dioecious trees in view with the tag, whatever its value). When it is missing on a tree of a dioecious species, the info panel shows an unknown-sex symbol next to the title.

Shown in the info panel (♂); clicking it shows the traits of male trees for some dioecious species. Suggested as a hint, with sex=female, for trees of those species without sex=*, in the season when the sex can be recognised.

Shown in the info panel (♀); clicking it shows the traits of female trees for some dioecious species. Suggested as a hint for Ginkgo biloba trees without sex=*, in the season when female trees bear seeds, and, with sex=male, for trees of the other dioecious species with known traits, in the season when the sex can be recognised.
Used for QA checks (a monumental tree should have denotation=natural_monument).
Treated as denotation=natural_monument: used to render the trees, for QA checks and for the world map of monumental trees. Reported by a QA check when denotation=natural_monument is missing.
Shown in the info panel, with a link to the tree's page on baumkunde.de.
Shown in the info panel, with a link to the tree's page on mbreg.de.
Shown in the info panel, with links to the iNaturalist observations.
Reported by a QA check: the key for the MASAF code is ref:masaf.
Reported by a QA check: the key for the ÚSOP code is ref:usop.
Reported by a QA check: the key for the ÚSOP code is ref:usop.
Used to render sacred trees (zapis) and to name them in the info panel.
Used to render sacred trees.
Used to render sacred trees.
Used to render sacred trees and to name them (rag tree) in the info panel.
Draws several trunks instead of one (yes = 2, a number = that many, several circumferences = one trunk each) and is shown in the tree card.
Draws a ring of green dots around the trunk.

From 8 December to 6 January: draws blinking coloured lights and a yellow star on the crown (needleleaved if leaf_type is missing). Also downloaded when the node is not natural=tree, only for this rendering (no QA checks).
On trees: rendered as a sacred tree (goshinboku) and named in the info panel.
Used for QA checks and the info panel. A Wikipedia article is reported (articles go in wikipedia).
Used for QA checks and the info panel. A Wikipedia article is reported (articles go in wikipedia).
Suggested when image is the page of a Mapillary photo.
Used for QA checks, the info panel and to show a picture, which counts as a photo in the Completeness tab.
Used for QA checks and to show a picture; counts as a photo in the Completeness tab. Suggested when image points to a Wikimedia Commons file.
Used for QA checks and to show a picture; counts as a photo in the Completeness tab.

Used for QA checks and to show a picture; counts as a photo in the Completeness tab. A Wikimedia Commons file without wikimedia_commons gives a hint to replace it with wikimedia_commons; a web page (Mapillary, Flickr, Google Drive…; not Google Photos) instead of an image file gives a hint. image=File:… is shown as a Commons file and gives the same hint as other Commons files. For Google Photos links the shared photo is shown.
Used to show a picture; counts as a photo in the Completeness tab.
Used for QA checks.
Used for QA checks.
Used for hints about known tree imports (documented or not).
Used for a QA check: the value is shown in the info panel.
Used for a QA check, like fixme: the value is shown in the info panel.
Shown as a hint in the info panel.

Suggested in a hint when a tree with height, circumference, diameter or diameter_crown was last edited more than 10 years ago: it can be added after surveying the measurements again, even with the same values.

Shown in the info panel. Used for QA checks: when it is the common name of a species or genus (e.g. name=Roverella), species or genus is suggested if no taxon tag is present, and a different species or genus is reported.
Shown in brackets after the title of the info panel (e.g. "Quercus robur (1543)").

Used for a QA check (the article's Wikidata item is a taxon: species:wikipedia or, for a genus, genus:wikipedia is suggested). Suggested when website or url is a Wikipedia article about the tree; compared with a Wikipedia article in website or url.

Used for a QA check (invalid or future date); shown in the info panel, with the age of the tree (today minus the date); used for the oldest trees in the Record trees tab (dates of the same year are tied), where its year also selects a sentence about what happened that year. Compared with planted_date (QA check: different values).

Used in place of start_date when start_date is missing: shown in the info panel with the age of the tree, used for the oldest trees in the Record trees tab and for the sentence about that year. Used for QA checks (invalid or future date, in the same forms as start_date; value different from start_date).
Used for a QA check: synonym of planted_date, planted_date is suggested.
Used for a QA check: synonym of planted_date, planted_date is suggested.
Used for a QA check: synonym of planted_date, planted_date is suggested.
Used for a QA check: synonym of planted_date, planted_date is suggested.
Used for a QA check: with a value other than yes or no, synonym of planted_date, planted_date is suggested.
